implementerProof.how: Round two. Every command in the implementer's eleven-entry proof array was re-run independently at 865aa8d982bb6ea8208d98a556f5f65d034004dd (the code of 7e0a3d53a245da0c80f3c48b64aafc76c319b77e, since the pull request head is handoff-only), on a rig rebuilt from the pull request body and packages/envoy/scripts/README.md alone: nats-server v2.10.22 linux-amd64 from the official GitHub release into /tmp/bin, ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN for the Go tests and PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH for the e2e driver. The whole cmd/listener package minus the 15 container-only tests is green (ok 141.011s), internal/session (ok 7.066s), internal/integration (ok 97.114s) and the container-free set of internal/bus (ok 71.912s) likewise. bash scripts/e2e-local.sh is green on the real binary, with the bus-down send answered 503 in 3.502818 s carrying Retry-After: 1 and the real @legion/envoy-client raising EnvoyApiError 503 rather than timing out. Each of the six review-round-two claims was checked by mutating the fix back out and watching the named lock go red, not by reading the diff: the CI image scrape, the retry clock, the three causes, the denied publish, the deferral cap and the declined -a 127.0.0.1 are each recorded in proof below. The container-only skip sets were recomputed from each package's own call graph rather than taken on trust: exactly the 15 cmd/listener names the body gives, 52 in internal/bus, 2 in internal/session, none of them an acceptance test.

proof.criterion: Review round two, finding 1: the envoy-e2e-local job finds the NATS image again, so the e2e-local acceptance this change extends runs in CI instead of being skipped.
proof.surface: The workflow step's own command run verbatim against the driver, and scripts/e2e-local.test.sh, which runs that same sed as its fourth case.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && nats_image=$(sed -n 's/^nats_image="\([^"]*\)".*$/\1/p' scripts/e2e-local.sh); [ -n "$nats_image" ] || { echo '::error::no nats_image declaration at column 0 of scripts/e2e-local.sh'; exit 1; }; printf 'step would pull: %s\n' "$nats_image"; and bash scripts/e2e-local.test.sh
proof.observed: step would pull: mirror.gcr.io/library/nats:2.10-alpine. scripts/e2e-local.test.sh prints 4 PASS, the fourth 'the NATS image is declared once, where the workflow scrapes it: mirror.gcr.io/library/nats:2.10-alpine'. The job itself cannot be quoted settled here: at the code head 7e0a3d53a245 the Legion Envoy and Contracts run 40170030066, which carries envoy-e2e-local, was still queued when this handoff was written, with Tests 40170030025 in progress and Docs 40170030019 and Worker Image 40170030038 success. A tester cites a lane that has not settled and does not wait for it; the mechanism the lane depends on is proven by the two mutations below instead.
proof.negativeControl: Two mutations, each the real regression. Inlining the image back into the docker run line, with the declaration left standing, fails the case: 'ERR: the docker run line of .../scripts/e2e-local.sh does not start $nats_image (mirror.gcr.io/library/nats:2.10-alpine)', exit 1. Deleting the declaration as well - the state the job actually failed in - fails it with 'ERR: no nats_image declaration at column 0', and the workflow step's own command then prints '::error::no nats_image declaration at column 0 of scripts/e2e-local.sh' and exits 1. Both reverted; the tree carries neither.

proof.criterion: Review round two, finding 2: the retry window is counted from the message's first delivery, not from the time JetStream stored it, so a backlog replayed into a cold cache is retried rather than given up at once.
proof.surface: A real JetStream durable over the notification stream on a real nats-server, running the listener's own jetStreamDeliveryHandler, with the envelope left to age past the window before its consumer exists.
proof.observed: --- PASS (14.77s), all three subtests: 'a window retries, then gives up once' PASS (5.58s), 'a zero window gives up on the first delivery' PASS (0.10s), 'a message older than the window is still deferred on its first delivery' PASS (9.10s).
proof.negativeControl: Mutating delivery.go:756 back to the old clock - `time.Since(metadata.Timestamp) < cfg.unplaceableRetryWindow` in place of `metadata.NumDelivered <= windowDeferrals` - fails two of the three subtests: the aged message with 'timed out waiting for the aged message's first delivery to be deferred', and the one-deferral window with '2 deferral lines, want exactly one - a window of one deferral defers the first delivery only'. The architect's concern that the replacement might pass for the wrong reason is answered by that second failure: the test discriminates the two clocks in both directions, not just on the aged message. Mutation reverted.

proof.criterion: Review round two, findings 5 and 6: each of the three unplaceable causes is deferred at attempt 1 under its own reason and given up under its own label, on a real durable at a real window, and a push that failed on the wire is no longer recorded as a record that names nothing to push to.
proof.surface: The same real durable over a real nats-server, four targets on one harness, the handler built at oneDeferralWindow from the harness's configuration.
proof.observed: --- PASS (5.11s). no_session_record/unplaceable_no_record, no_push_target/unplaceable_no_push_target and push_failed/unplaceable_push_failed each deferred then given up once under its own pair, the self-subscribed Port == 0 record still a delivered outcome, and 'listener agent session not found anywhere' nowhere in the log.
proof.negativeControl: The architect's question - whether this test could prove nothing the way its predecessor did - is answered by putting the predecessor's condition back: with cfg.unplaceableRetryWindow set to 0 in place of oneDeferralWindow the test fails, 'timed out waiting for every unplaceable cause to be deferred' after 20.66s. It cannot pass at a zero window. Mutation reverted.

proof.criterion: Review round two, findings 3 and 4: a publish the listener's own grant denies is answered 403 with no Retry-After and recorded for what it is, and the real client does not retry it; a lost role-claim race says so rather than blaming the bus; and 413, 400 and the genuine bus-unavailable 503 are unchanged beside them.
proof.surface: Three. S1: the publish route driven against a real nats-server started with a publish deny on one role subject, so the denial is the server's own permissions violation rather than a constructed error. S2: the repository's own tests for the two refusals. S3: the real @legion/envoy-client from packages/envoy-client, driven against each status.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && ENVOY_PROBE_NATS_URL='nats://probe:probe@127.0.0.1:14333' go test ./cmd/listener -run '^TestProbeGenuinelyDeniedPublish$' -count=1 -v (a throwaway probe, since removed, against a nats-server run with `publish: { deny: ["notifications.role.denied-probe"] }`); then go test ./cmd/listener -run '^(TestAPublishThatLosesTheRoleClaimRaceSaysSoRatherThanBlamingTheBus|TestADeniedPublishIsRefusedPermanentlyAndNotRecordedAsBusUnavailable)$' -count=1 -v; then bun run a script in packages/envoy-client that serves each status from a local server and counts the client's HTTP attempts
proof.observed: S1, a genuinely denied publish: status 403, no Retry-After header at all, body 'envoy: the message bus denied the publish under this listener's own permissions: bus: NATS denied the publish to "notifications.role.denied-probe": nats: permissions violation: Permissions Violation for Publish to "notifications.role.denied-probe"', and one WARN 'listener publish' line carrying outcome "publish_denied", status 403, topic and holder. S2: both tests PASS (0.97s, 0.00s) with all four subtests. S3, the real client: 403 -> 1 HTTP attempt in 19 ms, 413 -> 1 attempt, 400 -> 1 attempt, 503 -> 2 attempts in 253 ms. Moving the denied publish below 500 is what stops the retry, and transport.ts:281-284 is the rule it turns on.
proof.negativeControl: The same denied-publish probe, on the same connection and in the same run, publishes to notifications.role.allowed-probe - a role the server's deny list does not name - and is answered 200 with one INFO 'listener publish' line, outcome "accepted", holder named. So the 403 is the server's deny list and not the rig. The client's 503 case is the control for the retry: two attempts where the 403 takes one.

proof.criterion: Review round two, finding 7: deferrals cannot exhaust the durable's MaxAckPending budget, at the cap and one below it.
proof.surface: The listener's delivery handler against a real nats-server over a real durable, the handler's deferral counter preloaded, plus the arithmetic the cap rests on.
proof.observed: All PASS. At the cap (unplaceableDeferralCap = consumerMaxAckPending/4 = 64) the message is given up at once with its own ordinary record, no deferral line, no NAK, and the count returns to the cap; one slot below it the same message is deferred at attempt 1 and the count reaches the cap. TestUnplaceableRetryWindowFitsTheBoundsItDependsOn pins unplaceableDeferralCap*2 < consumerMaxAckPending beside the MaxDeliver and attempt-cache relations. The starvation question: 64 held deferrals leave 192 of the durable's 256 pending slots for traffic that lands on its first attempt, and the one way the count under-reports - a restart forgetting deferrals it was holding, which the code documents - costs at most one extra generation of 64, which is exactly the margin cap*2 < MaxAckPending reserves; a redelivery arriving for a message the new process never deferred releases nothing below zero.
proof.negativeControl: Two. The cap test's own pair differs in one field, the preloaded count. And the slot-release half, which nothing pinned: deleting the release on redelivery (delivery.go:629-631) left every delivery test green, so I added TestARedeliveryGivesItsDeferralSlotBack, which fails under that deletion with 'timed out waiting for the redelivery of the deferred message to be deferred again' and passes at head in 10.38s. Recorded below.

proof.criterion: Review round two, the declined minor: the local test server's open port is closed by a drawn password rather than by -a 127.0.0.1, and internal/bus is green.
proof.surface: The repository's own suites, and the code the declination rests on.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN=/tmp/bin/nats-server go test ./internal/bus -count=1 -skip <the 52 container-taking tests, recomputed from the package's call graph>; and go test ./internal/session ./internal/integration -count=1 -skip '^(TestStopWatchIsFinal|TestStopWatchMakesNoRequestOfTheServer)$'
proof.observed: ok internal/bus 71.912s, ok internal/session 7.066s, ok internal/integration 97.114s. The reasoning holds: internal/bus/remote_nats_test.go:254-266 reads net.InterfaceAddrs() and skips when the machine has no non-loopback IPv4 address to reach the test server by, so -a 127.0.0.1 would make that guard untestable. What replaces it is a 128-bit password drawn once per test binary (crypto/rand, internal/testnats/nats.go accountSecret) shared by every account, in place of the account's own name, which anything reaching the port could have guessed. My judgement: the exposure is closed. The port is still bound on every interface, but it now wants a secret no one can guess, it exists only while one test binary runs, it holds nothing but that binary's own JetStream, and it is reached only through ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN, which CI never sets.
proof.negativeControl: The two container-taking tests of internal/session and the 52 of internal/bus were identified by call graph, not by name, and each package's remainder is green; a test hidden behind a skip would have to be one no path reaches testnats.Start* or testcontainers through.

proof.criterion: A1 to A6, the issue's own acceptance, re-driven at this head after the review's changes.
proof.surface: Both. S1: the listener's two HTTP routes and its JetStream delivery handler against a real nats-server. S2: the real envoy-listener binary under scripts/e2e-local.sh.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN=/tmp/bin/nats-server go test ./cmd/listener -count=1 -skip <the 15 container-only tests>; and PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH bash scripts/e2e-local.sh
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/listener 141.011s, which includes every acceptance test of rounds one and two. The e2e prints both PASS lines; out/e2e/listener.log, read field by field, carries exactly seven request records - INFO listener send ses_e2e_local accepted 200; WARN listener send ses_e2e_local_absent no_live_session 404; WARN listener publish notifications.role.e2e-reviewer role_unclaimed 404 with no holder; INFO listener publish notifications.role.e2e-reviewer accepted 200 holder ses_e2e_local; and three WARN listener send bus_unavailable 503 for the bus-down curl and the real client's two attempts - with the bus-down send answered in 3.502818 s and Retry-After: 1.
proof.negativeControl: The e2e's own pair: the absent destination is 404 {"error":"no live session ses_e2e_local_absent"} against the same live bus that answers the accepted send 200, so the refusals are the destinations' doing and not the rig's. Round one's api.go:706 control still stands at this head through TestSendRefusesTheBusRatherThanTheSessionWhenTheStoreReadDoesNotAnswer, which is in the package run above.

regressionLocksAdded.why: unplaceableDeferralCap counts the messages the handler holds deferred right now, and releaseDeferredUnplaceable gives a slot back when the redelivery arrives (delivery.go:629-631). Nothing pinned that release: the cap's own test preloads the count and reads it after one disposition, and every other unplaceable test runs far from the cap, so deleting the release left the whole delivery suite green. A leaked slot is permanent, so after 64 deferrals the handler would defer nothing again, give every unplaceable message up on its first delivery, and say nothing about why - the retry quietly ceasing, which is the shape of failure this issue exists to end. The new test starts one slot under the cap with a two-deferral window, so the second deferral is possible only if the redelivery released the first; it fails under the deletion with 'timed out waiting for the redelivery of the deferred message to be deferred again' and passes at head in 10.38s, reading the count back at both ends as its control.

The send route's status map row for a session read that did not answer had no lock: mutating api.go:706 to answer 404 for every read error left the suite green. Still green at this head, inside the package run recorded above.
